newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico reserves, net assets up to April 4.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico reserves, net assets up to April 4.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its net international assets as of April 4 were $11.165 billion, compared to $10.683 billion on March 26.
The central bank said that its international reserves as of April 4 were $20.510 billion, compared to $19.836 billion as of March 26.
The central bank said the increase of $482 million in net international assets in the same time period was due to:
--Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $214 million.

--The purchase of $220 million from credit institutions, a product of the partial exercising of options on the sale of dollars to the central bank that were issued during the auction of February and March.
--Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $28 million.

--A net gain of $20 million dollars for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that the monetary base fell by 5.203 billion pesos due to a fall in the seasonal demand of bills and coins.
The balance of federal government deposits rose 4.853 billion pesos due to tax collections, the central bank said.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.

*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
